# Control Narrative: Sanitary Lift Station LS-12

**Status:** DRAFT for Engineer of Record and Owner review.
**Convention:** Values marked **[A]** are defaults the operator can adjust from SCADA within the limits in Section 11. Items marked **⚠ OPEN** need a decision before programming is final. Section 16 summarizes them.

---

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This narrative defines the control, monitoring, alarm, and fallback functions for LS-12. It covers:
- PLC logic
- Hardwired backup circuits
- VFD configuration that affects control
- SCADA interface

It is the basis for PLC programming and for the Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) in Section 15.

**Overriding objective:** Prevent wet well overflow at 2.8 m. Overflow discharges to a creek and is a permit violation. Where availability and equipment protection conflict, this narrative favors keeping a pump running, except for dry-run protection (LSL-121).

## 2. Basis and Assumptions

1. **Level datum:** 0.00 m is the wet well floor. LIT-121 is zeroed to that datum. If the transducer's sensing point is above the floor, apply an offset in the PLC scaling. The station cannot measure level below the sensing point.
2. LIT-121 output is 4–20 mA, linear over 0–3.0 m.
3. Each VFD receives:
   - a hardwired run command (DO)
   - a 4–20 mA speed reference (AO), scaled 4 mA = 0 Hz and 20 mA = 60 Hz.
4. Each VFD returns running status, fault status, and Local/Remote status (DI).
5. **⚠ OPEN:** I/O items 2–4 assume hardwired signals. If the integrator proposes a network connection, it must still include hardwired run/backup paths.
6. Each pump has a motor protection relay (thermal and seal/moisture). The relay trips the VFD directly through hardwiring and gives a status contact to the PLC. **⚠ OPEN:** Confirm against the pump submittal.
7. The PLC, radio, and float backup control power are on a UPS that rides through generator start and transfer. Minimum backup time: **⚠ OPEN**, 2 hours suggested.
8. Wet well geometry and inflow have not been provided to this author. Cycle-time checks are listed in Section 16.

## 3. Equipment and I/O

### 3.1 Equipment

| Tag | Description |
|---|---|
| P-121, P-122 | Submersible sewage pumps, each 100% duty, on VFD-121 and VFD-122 |
| LIT-121 | Submersible pressure transducer, 0–3.0 m |
| LSL-121 | Low-level float, 0.4 m. Dry-run protection |
| LSHH-121 | High-high float, 2.6 m. Backup control and alarm |
| HS-121, HS-122 | Hand-Off-Auto switches at the MCC |
| ATS / GEN | Automatic transfer switch and standby generator |
| PLC / RTU | Station PLC with licensed radio to central SCADA |

### 3.2 Minimum PLC I/O (per pump unless noted)

- **DI, per pump:**
  - HOA in Auto
  - HOA in Hand
  - VFD Running
  - VFD Fault
  - VFD in Remote
  - Motor Protection Trip (overtemp/seal)
- **DI, station:**
  - LSL-121 (state)
  - LSHH-121 (state)
  - Float Backup Run Active
  - Utility Power OK (phase monitor)
  - ATS in Normal
  - ATS in Emergency
  - Generator Running
  - Generator Common Fault
  - Generator Low Fuel
  - UPS On Battery
  - UPS Fault
  - Wet well hatch/intrusion (**⚠ OPEN**, optional)
- **DO:**
  - Run command (per pump)
  - VFD fault reset (per pump, optional)
  - PLC watchdog relay
  - Local alarm beacon
- **AI:**
  - LIT-121
  - VFD speed feedback (per pump, optional)
  - Motor current (per pump, optional)
- **AO:**
  - VFD speed reference (per pump)

**Float wiring convention:**
- **LSL-121:** The contact is closed when level is above 0.4 m (permissive). A broken wire therefore stops pumps in Auto and Hand. That failure is detected by the discrepancy alarm in Section 5.3.
- **LSHH-121:** The contact closes when level rises to 2.6 m.
- **⚠ OPEN:** Confirm this convention with the Owner.

## 4. Setpoints and Timers

### 4.1 Level setpoints

| Function | Level (m) | LIT mA | Adjustable |
|---|---|---|---|
| LSL-121 float (dry-run cutoff) | 0.40 | 6.133 | No (physical) |
| Lead stop | 0.60 | 7.200 | [A] |
| Lag stop **⚠ OPEN**, proposed | 1.40 | 11.467 | [A] |
| Lead start (speed ramp begins) | 1.60 | 12.533 | [A] |
| Lag start (speed ramp ends) | 2.00 | 14.667 | [A] |
| High level alarm, ON / OFF | 2.30 / 2.20 | 16.267 / 15.733 | [A] |
| LSHH-121 float (backup run, alarm) | 2.60 | 17.867 | No (physical) |
| Overflow (event logging, alarm) | 2.80 | 18.933 | No (fixed by structure) |
| Overflow event end | 2.70 | 18.400 | [A] |

LIT conversion: mA = 4 + 16 × L / 3.0, and L = (mA − 4) × 3.0 / 16.

### 4.2 Timers (all [A])

| Timer | Default |
|---|---|
| LIT input filter (first-order time constant) | 3 s |
| Float debounce (each float, each direction) | 2 s |
| Lead start delay (level ≥ lead start) | 5 s |
| Lag start delay (level ≥ lag start) | 10 s |
| Stop delays (lead or lag) | 3 s |
| Fail-to-start (run command, no Running feedback) | 15 s |
| High level alarm delay | 10 s |
| Lead-to-lag start stagger (any simultaneous call) | 10 s |
| Restart delay after power restored | 10 s |
| LIT discrepancy delay | 60 s |
| Excessive continuous run alarm | 60 min |
| Excessive starts alarm (per pump, rolling 1 h) | 10 starts |
| SCADA comm fail (PLC side, no poll received) | 5 min |

Stop delays must never delay a start on rising level beyond the values above.

## 5. Level Measurement and Validation

### 5.1 Scaling and filtering

1. Scale LIT-121 to 0.00–3.00 m.
2. Apply the filter from Section 4.2.
3. Use the filtered value for all control decisions.
4. Report both raw and filtered values to SCADA.

### 5.2 Transducer fault (LIT FAIL)

LIT FAIL is declared on either condition:
- Signal < 3.6 mA or > 21.0 mA for 5 s (NAMUR NE43 limits).
- Analog channel diagnostic fault.

On LIT FAIL:
1. Raise alarm **LIT-121 FAIL**.
2. Stop level-based PLC control. Hold no pump commands from level.
3. Control passes to float backup (Section 8).
4. Pumps already running under PLC control continue at 60 Hz until LSL-121 opens. Then they stop.
5. After that, operation is float-only until LIT FAIL clears and the operator resets it.

**⚠ OPEN:** Should LIT FAIL clear automatically when the signal returns, or require an operator reset? This draft assumes operator reset.

### 5.3 Discrepancy checks

Each check below must persist for the discrepancy delay.

- **LSHH-121 active while LIT < 2.40 m:** Alarm "LIT/LSHH DISCREPANCY". This means either LIT is reading low (dangerous) or the float is stuck. Do not change control. The float backup is already acting.
- **LSL-121 open (low) while LIT > 0.80 m:** Alarm "LIT/LSL DISCREPANCY". This means a stuck or failed float, or a broken wire. Pumps will be blocked by the interlock, so this alarm is High priority.
- **LIT ≥ 2.70 m while LSHH-121 is not active:** Alarm "LSHH-121 FAIL SUSPECT".

## 6. Control Modes

### 6.1 HOA = OFF
- The pump cannot run in any mode, including float backup.
- The pump is unavailable to the PLC.
- Status goes to SCADA.

### 6.2 HOA = HAND
1. The VFD runs through a hardwired circuit that is independent of the PLC.
2. Speed is the VFD's local preset (Preset Speed 1). **⚠ OPEN:** default 60 Hz.
3. The hardwired LSL-121 interlock (Section 9) stops the pump.
4. The pump is unavailable to PLC Auto.
5. PLC alarm "P-12x NOT IN AUTO" is set, as an event or low priority.

**⚠ OPEN:** Should Hand bypass LSL-121 for wet well cleaning? This draft keeps the interlock in Hand.

### 6.3 HOA = AUTO, VFD in Remote
- The pump is controlled by the PLC (Section 7) or by float backup (Section 8).
- If the VFD is in Local/Keypad while the HOA is in Auto, the pump is unavailable. Alarm "VFD-12x NOT IN REMOTE".

### 6.4 Pump Available (for PLC lead/lag)

A pump is available when **all** of the following are true:
- HOA in Auto
- VFD in Remote
- No VFD Fault
- No Motor Protection Trip
- No PLC pump-fail latch (Section 7.5)
- Not placed Out of Service from SCADA

## 7. Normal Automatic Control (PLC)

### 7.1 Lead/lag assignment
- The PLC keeps a lead pointer: P-121 or P-122.
- The other available pump is lag.
- If only one pump is available, it is lead and there is no lag.
- The pointer and the pump-fail latches are retained through power loss.

### 7.2 Lead pump
- **Start:** Filtered level ≥ lead start (1.60 m) for the lead start delay.
- **Stop:** Level ≤ lead stop (0.60 m) for the stop delay.
- Between those points the lead keeps its current state (hysteresis).

### 7.3 Lead speed

While the lead runs and the lag is off:

```
f = 45 + (60 − 45) × (L − LeadStart) / (LagStart − LeadStart)
  = 45 + 37.5 × (L − 1.60)              [with default setpoints]
f clamped to 45.0 ≤ f ≤ 60.0 Hz
```

- Below 1.60 m (drawing down toward lead stop), speed is 45 Hz.
- At 2.00 m and above, speed is 60 Hz.
- The formula uses the current setpoints, so it stays correct if they are changed.

Check values:

| Level (m) | Speed (Hz) | AO (mA) |
|---|---|---|
| 1.60 | 45.0 | 16.0 |
| 1.80 | 52.5 | 18.0 |
| 2.00 | 60.0 | 20.0 |

**⚠ OPEN:** Confirm that 45 Hz is above shutoff against static head at the lowest wet well level. It must also give at least 0.6 m/s scour velocity in the force main. See Section 16.

### 7.4 Lag pump
- **Start:** Level ≥ lag start (2.00 m) for the lag start delay.
- **Stop:** Level ≤ lag stop (1.40 m) for the stop delay.
- While the lag runs, **both pumps run at 60 Hz**. When the lag stops, the lead returns to the Section 7.3 formula.
- **⚠ OPEN:** Lag stop setpoint and dual-pump speed strategy were not specified by Operations. Both are proposed here.

### 7.5 Pump failure in Auto

A pump is failed when any of these occur:
- **Fail-to-start:** Run command present and no Running feedback within 15 s.
- **Run feedback lost:** Running feedback lost while the command is present (1 s).
- VFD Fault.
- Motor Protection Trip.

On failure:
1. Remove the run command.
2. Set the PLC fail latch for that pump.
3. Raise the alarm.
4. Promote the other available pump to lead immediately.
5. If the level calls for a pump, start the promoted pump without waiting for the start delay.
6. The failed pump stays unavailable until the fail latch is reset. Reset requires the cause to be cleared and an operator reset from local HMI or SCADA. **⚠ OPEN:** Is SCADA reset allowed?

### 7.6 Alternation
1. **Cycle definition:** One pump cycle ends when the lead pump stops normally, either at lead stop or by the LSL interlock.
2. **At the end of each cycle,** toggle the lead pointer to the other pump if that pump is available. If it is not available, keep the current lead.
3. **Failure promotions** (Section 7.5) change the pointer but do not count as a cycle.
4. **SCADA commands:**
   - "Alternation Enable/Disable"
   - "Lead Select" (P-121 or P-122), allowed when alternation is disabled
   - "Force Alternate", which takes effect at the next cycle end

### 7.7 Both pumps unavailable

If neither pump is available in Auto, raise **NO PUMPS AVAILABLE** (Critical). This alarm is active regardless of level. Float backup still operates any pump that is in Auto with a healthy VFD.

## 8. Float Backup Control (Hardwired)

This circuit runs pumps without the PLC. It protects against PLC failure, LIT failure, or logic failure.

1. **Trigger:** LSHH-121 closes (2.6 m). A hardwired latch relay energizes "Float Backup Run".
2. **VFD-121:** Float Backup Run, through the P-121 HOA Auto contact, drives a VFD digital input. That input commands **Run at Preset Speed 2 (60 Hz)** and overrides the PLC run and speed reference.
3. **VFD-122:** Receives the same signal through a hardwired on-delay relay of 10 s **[A at relay]**. This staggers starts on generator power.
4. **Latch release:** The latch clears only when LSL-121 opens (level below 0.4 m). Pumps then stop. The latch does not release when LSHH-121 resets.
5. **PLC role:** The PLC monitors LSHH-121 and Float Backup Run Active.
   - LSHH-121 raises **HIGH-HIGH LEVEL** (Critical).
   - Float Backup Run Active raises **FLOAT BACKUP ACTIVE** (High).
   - The PLC does not inhibit the backup circuit.
6. **Pumps excluded from backup:**
   - Pumps with HOA in Off or Hand.
   - Pumps with a VFD fault or motor protection trip, because the VFD will not run.

**Power source:** The backup circuit is powered from UPS-backed 24 VDC control power. It must work with the PLC powered down.

**⚠ OPEN:** Pumping down to 0.4 m during backup operation needs 0.4 m to meet the pump manufacturer's minimum submergence (Section 16).

## 9. Interlocks

| Interlock | Implementation | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| LSL-121 low (< 0.4 m) | **Hardwired** in the run circuit of both VFDs. Also monitored by the PLC | Stops pumps in Auto, Hand, and Float Backup. Clears float backup latch |
| Motor protection trip | Hardwired to VFD (safe torque off or run interlock) | Stops pump. PLC fail latch |
| VFD fault | VFD internal | Stops pump. PLC fail latch |
| HOA Off | Hardwired | Pump cannot run |

LSL-121 also generates PLC alarm **LOW LEVEL** (Medium) when it opens while a pump has a run command. This indicates the lead stop was missed.

## 10. Power Failure and Standby Generator

1. **Utility loss:**
   - The PLC sees Utility Power OK go false.
   - The PLC remains powered by the UPS.
   - Alarm **UTILITY POWER FAIL** (High).
   - The PLC removes all pump run commands while VFD power is absent.
   - The PLC keeps the level state and lead pointer.
2. **Generator start and transfer:**
   - The ATS starts the generator and transfers.
   - The PLC reports Generator Running and ATS in Emergency.
3. **Pump restart on generator:**
   - When ATS is in Emergency and Generator Running, the PLC waits the restart delay (10 s).
   - The PLC then resumes normal logic.
   - If both pumps are called, the lag starts at least 10 s after the lead (stagger timer).
4. **Retransfer to utility:**
   - Any interruption during retransfer repeats step 3.
   - Restart timing is the same in both directions.
5. **Generator alarms:**
   - Generator Common Fault (High)
   - Generator Low Fuel (High)
   - Generator Fail to Start: ATS in Emergency is not reached within 60 s of utility loss (Critical)
6. **UPS alarms:** UPS On Battery (Medium) and UPS Fault (High).
7. **Generator sizing:** **⚠ OPEN.** Confirm that the generator can run both pumps at 60 Hz with VFD harmonic loading. This is the high-level condition, and it is the most likely operating case during a storm outage.

## 11. SCADA Interface

### 11.1 Communications
- The PLC operates fully autonomously. Loss of communications has no effect on pump control.
- **SCADA side:** Alarm **LS-12 COMM FAIL** (High) after the configured number of missed polls. **⚠ OPEN:** Define the poll rate and count.
- **PLC side:** Set a local comm-fail flag after 5 minutes without a poll, and light the local beacon.
- **PLC event buffer:**
  - The PLC keeps a time-stamped buffer of alarms and events, with at least 500 entries.
  - It backfills SCADA when communications return.
  - Overflow events must never be lost to a communications outage.
- **Time sync:** The PLC clock is synchronized from SCADA daily.

### 11.2 Monitoring points

Report all DI, AI, and alarms listed in this document, plus:
- Lead pointer
- Pump run hours and starts (each pump, retained)
- Starts in the last hour
- Commanded speed and feedback speed
- Station mode, including Float Backup Active

### 11.3 Remote commands
- Setpoint changes
- Alternation enable/disable
- Lead select
- Force alternate
- Pump Out of Service / Return to Service
- PLC fail-latch reset (**⚠ OPEN**)
- Alarm acknowledge

No remote manual start or stop of pumps is provided in this draft. **⚠ OPEN:** Does the Owner want it?

### 11.4 Setpoint validation

The PLC rejects any setpoint write that violates either of these rules:

```
0.50 ≤ LeadStop < LagStop < LeadStart < LagStart < HighAlarmOn ≤ 2.50
Each adjacent pair at least 0.10 m apart. HighAlarmOff < HighAlarmOn.
```

A rejected write:
- leaves the previous value in place,
- logs the event "SETPOINT REJECTED" with the attempted value.

Setpoints are retained in nonvolatile memory.

## 12. Alarms

| Alarm | Condition | Delay | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| OVERFLOW | LIT ≥ 2.80 m | 0 s | Critical, regulatory |
| HIGH-HIGH LEVEL | LSHH-121 active | 2 s debounce | Critical |
| NO PUMPS AVAILABLE | Section 7.7 | 5 s | Critical |
| GENERATOR FAIL TO START | Section 10 | 60 s | Critical |
| HIGH LEVEL | LIT ≥ 2.30 m, clears ≤ 2.20 m | 10 s | High |
| FLOAT BACKUP ACTIVE | Backup latch on | 0 s | High |
| LIT-121 FAIL | Section 5.2 | 5 s | High |
| LIT/LSL DISCREPANCY | Section 5.3 | 60 s | High |
| P-12x FAIL | Section 7.5 (each pump, with cause) | per 7.5 | High |
| UTILITY POWER FAIL | Phase monitor | 2 s | High |
| GENERATOR FAULT / LOW FUEL | DI | 2 s | High |
| COMM FAIL | Section 11.1 | per 11.1 | High (SCADA) |
| UPS FAULT | DI | 5 s | High |
| LIT/LSHH DISCREPANCY, LSHH FAIL SUSPECT | Section 5.3 | 60 s | Medium |
| LOW LEVEL | Section 9 | 2 s | Medium |
| P-12x EXCESSIVE RUN TIME | Continuous run > 60 min | none | Medium |
| P-12x EXCESSIVE STARTS | > 10 starts in rolling 1 h | none | Medium |
| UPS ON BATTERY | DI | 5 s | Medium |
| P-12x NOT IN AUTO / VFD NOT IN REMOTE | DI | 5 s | Low |

Alarm behavior:
- Alarms latch until acknowledged and the condition clears.
- Critical and High alarms light the local beacon.

## 13. Overflow Event Recording

- **Event start:** LIT ≥ 2.80 m. The PLC records a time-stamped start.
- **Event end:** LIT ≤ 2.70 m for 60 s. The PLC records a time-stamped end.
- **Recorded data:** Start time, end time, duration, peak level, pump status during the event, and power source during the event.
- **Retention:** At least 50 events, held in nonvolatile memory.
- **Reporting:** Events are reported to SCADA for permit reporting.
- **Limitations:**
  - Overflow volume is not calculated. The station has no overflow flow measurement.
  - If LIT-121 has failed, the PLC cannot detect overflow.

**⚠ OPEN:** Strongly recommend an independent overflow sensor, such as a float at 2.8 m or a sensor in the overflow pipe, wired to the PLC.

## 14. PLC Startup and Failure

- **On power-up:**
  - Retain setpoints, lead pointer, fail latches, and counters.
  - Hold run commands off for the restart delay.
  - Then resume Auto logic.
- **Watchdog:**
  - The PLC pulses the watchdog relay.
  - If the PLC halts, the watchdog drops out and lights the local beacon.
  - SCADA will raise COMM FAIL.
  - Float backup (Section 8) remains in effect.
- **Analog outputs on PLC fault:** Configure them to fail to 20 mA (60 Hz). The run commands drop out, and backup operation is through the hardwired path only.

## 15. Factory Acceptance Test

### 15.1 Test setup
- Simulate LIT-121 with a calibrated 4–20 mA source.
- Simulate floats, HOA, ATS, generator, and UPS contacts with switches.
- Use the actual VFDs, or VFD simulators that return Running feedback and accept Run and preset inputs.
- Measure speed references with a calibrated mA meter.
- Use a SCADA test station or a radio test link.

### 15.2 Initial conditions (unless a test says otherwise)
- Both HOA switches in Auto.
- Both VFDs in Remote.
- No faults.
- P-121 is lead.
- LIT at 0.50 m (6.667 mA).
- LSL-121 closed (above).
- LSHH-121 open.
- Utility power OK.

### 15.3 Tests

| # | Test | Action | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | LIT scaling | Inject 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 mA | 0.00, 0.75, 1.50, 2.25, 3.00 m (±0.01 m) at HMI and SCADA |
| 2 | LIT fail | Inject 3.5 mA, then 21.5 mA | LIT-121 FAIL after 5 s each time. No PLC-initiated starts |
| 3 | Lead start | Raise to 1.59 m (12.48 mA), then 1.60 m (12.533 mA) | No start at 1.59. P-121 starts 5 s after 1.60. AO = 16.0 mA (45 Hz) |
| 4 | Speed ramp | Raise to 1.80 m (13.60 mA), then 2.00 m (14.667 mA) | AO 18.0 mA (52.5 Hz), then 20.0 mA (60 Hz) |
| 5 | Lead stop and alternation | Lower to 1.00 m (9.333 mA), then 0.60 m (7.20 mA) | 45 Hz at 1.00 m. P-121 stops 3 s after 0.60. Lead pointer changes to P-122 |
| 6 | Next cycle | Raise to 1.60 m | P-122 starts, not P-121 |
| 7 | Lag start | Raise to 2.00 m and hold | P-121 (lag) starts after 10 s. Both AOs at 20.0 mA |
| 8 | Lag stop | Lower to 1.40 m (11.467 mA) | Lag stops after 3 s. Lead continues at 45 Hz |
| 9 | High level alarm | Raise to 2.30 m (16.267 mA) for 10 s, then lower to 2.20 m (15.733 mA) | Alarm after 10 s. Clears at 2.20. Beacon on |
| 10 | Overflow event | Raise to 2.80 m (18.933 mA) for 2 min, then 2.70 m (18.40 mA) for 60 s | OVERFLOW alarm immediately. Event logged with start, end, duration, and peak level |
| 11 | Fail-to-start | Block P-122 Running feedback with P-122 lead, level 1.60 m | P-122 FAIL after 15 s. P-121 starts immediately. P-122 unavailable until reset |
| 12 | Fault while running | Assert VFD-121 Fault while P-121 runs | P-121 command drops. P-121 FAIL. P-122 starts immediately |
| 13 | Motor protection | Assert Motor Protection Trip on running pump | Same response as Test 12, with cause shown |
| 14 | HOA out of Auto | Place lead HOA to Off | Pump removed. NOT IN AUTO alarm. Other pump becomes lead |
| 15 | No pumps available | Both HOAs to Off | NO PUMPS AVAILABLE (Critical) after 5 s |
| 16 | VFD Local | Place VFD-121 in Local | Unavailable. VFD NOT IN REMOTE alarm |
| 17 | Hand mode | HOA-121 to Hand with PLC in Stop mode | P-121 runs at Preset 1 independent of PLC. Opening LSL-121 stops it |
| 18 | LSL interlock in Auto | Pump running at 1.00 m. Open LSL-121 | Pump stops (hardwired). LOW LEVEL alarm. LIT/LSL DISCREPANCY after 60 s |
| 19 | Float backup | LIT at 1.00 m and PLC in Stop (or powered off). Close LSHH-121 | P-121 runs at 60 Hz immediately. P-122 runs after 10 s |
| 20 | Backup latch | Continue from 19. Open LSHH-121, then open LSL-121 | Pumps keep running after LSHH-121 opens. Both stop when LSL-121 opens. Latch clears |
| 21 | Backup with PLC running | Repeat 19 with PLC running | HIGH-HIGH LEVEL and FLOAT BACKUP ACTIVE alarms. LIT/LSHH DISCREPANCY after 60 s |
| 22 | Backup exclusion | Repeat 19 with HOA-122 in Off | Only P-121 runs |
| 23 | LIT fail with floats | LIT at 3.5 mA, then cycle LSHH-121 and LSL-121 | Pumps run and stop on floats only |
| 24 | Power fail and generator | Pumps running. Drop Utility OK, then assert ATS Emergency and Gen Running | UTILITY POWER FAIL. Run commands off. Restart 10 s after ATS Emergency. Lag starts 10 s after lead |
| 25 | Generator fail to start | Drop Utility OK with no ATS Emergency | GENERATOR FAIL TO START after 60 s |
| 26 | Generator and UPS alarms | Assert each DI | Correct alarm, priority, and delay |
| 27 | Comm loss | Disconnect radio for 10 min with a level excursion | Control is unaffected. SCADA COMM FAIL. PLC beacon after 5 min. Buffered events backfill with original time stamps on reconnect |
| 28 | Setpoint validation | Write lead stop 0.30 m, then lead start 2.10 m | Both writes rejected. Previous values kept. SETPOINT REJECTED events logged |
| 29 | Valid setpoint change | Change lag start to 2.10 m | Accepted. Speed ramp now reaches 60 Hz at 2.10 m (1.85 m gives 52.5 Hz) |
| 30 | SCADA commands | Disable alternation, select lead, force alternate, set out of service, reset fail latch | Each behaves per Sections 7.6, 11.3, and 7.5 |
| 31 | Run time and starts | Hold lead running for more than 60 min (timer may be shortened for test). Cycle lead more than 10 times in 1 h | EXCESSIVE RUN TIME and EXCESSIVE STARTS alarms |
| 32 | PLC power cycle | Power cycle the PLC | Setpoints, lead pointer, fail latches, counters, and overflow log retained. Restart delay observed |
| 33 | Watchdog | Halt PLC | Watchdog relay drops. Beacon on. Float backup still functional (repeat Test 19) |

Restore the initial conditions after each test. Record actual values, times, and pass/fail.

## 16. Open Items and Engineering Checks

1. **Lag stop setpoint and dual-pump speed** (proposed: 1.40 m and both at 60 Hz). Operations to confirm.
2. **45 Hz minimum speed.** Verify against the pump curve and system curve at the 0.6 m lead stop. Check:
   - flow exceeds shutoff,
   - force main velocity is at least 0.6 m/s,
   - operation stays within the manufacturer's allowable operating region.
3. **Submergence.** Confirm that 0.6 m (normal) and 0.4 m (backup and LSL) meet the pump's minimum submergence for motor cooling and vortex prevention.
4. **Cycle time.** Using wet well area and peak/average inflow, check the starts per hour for the 0.6 to 1.6 m band against the motor limit. Alternation halves starts per pump. Also check the low-inflow case, where 45 Hz capacity is much greater than inflow.
5. **Independent overflow sensor.** Strongly recommended (Section 13).
6. **Float contact convention** and **LSL interlock in Hand** (Sections 3.2 and 6.2).
7. **Hand-mode speed** (Preset 1) and **backup speed** (Preset 2, 60 Hz).
8. **Remote controls.** Decide on SCADA fail-latch reset and remote manual start.
9. **Generator sizing** for both pumps on VFDs.
10. **SCADA poll rate and comm-fail count.**
11. **Motor protection relay I/O** per the pump submittal.
12. **LIT installation.** Confirm the mounting elevation and offset relative to the 0.00 m datum.
13. **Time stamps.** Confirm that overflow time-stamp resolution and retention meet the permit's reporting requirements.
